correctness.rationale: The representative facet x+y=2 has perpendicular diagonals 2 and 2sqrt(2); summing over the 12 signed-pair facets by Cauchy's formula gives 4(2a+b). The minimum inequality has equality only at a=b=c, and the upper Cauchy–Schwarz equality gives (2,1,0)/sqrt(5). The chamber's solid-angle density in (s,t) is s/(1+s²+s²t²)^(3/2); clipping in t is correct up to null boundaries. The first-order excess at (s,t)=(1,1) is 4((1-s)+(1-t))/sqrt(3); the density is constant to leading order, giving the triangular area, the coefficient sqrt(3)/(8pi), and the normalized uniform simplex limit. For the cap count, (2,1,0) has exactly the three neighbors (2,0,±1) and (1,2,0) at dot product 4; they do not neighbor one another. Thus there are 36 first pairs and no local triple intersections. For a nearest pair put the centers at (C,±S,0), with C=3/sqrt(10), S=1/sqrt(10), R=4sqrt(5). In the chart U=(sqrt(1-y²-z²),y,z), at height x=RC-h the lens is C sqrt(1-y²-z²)-S|y|≥C-h/R. Setting d=h/R, its half-width in z is asymptotically sqrt(2(d-S|y|)/C), for |y| up to d/S+O(d²). Factoring the squared half-width at its simple zero and rescaling gives area 8 sqrt(2/C) d^(3/2)/(3S)+O(d^(5/2)). Multiplying by 36/(4pi) gives the claimed correction. Above contact the caps have disjoint interiors, and just below they overlap on positive area, proving maximality. The mean is 12(2sqrt(2))/4=6sqrt(2), exactly the contact value. An independent height–azimuth quadrature and center enumeration reproduced the cap count, linear tail, endpoint scaling and numerical median.
residual_risks: The independent quadrature is diagnostic, not an interval certificate. The analytic proof supplies the exact constants. Later cap-contact regimes are not classified.
